question: The "emoluments, allowances, and privileges of constitutional officeholders" are governed under which schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions relating to **emoluments, allowances, and privileges of constitutional officeholders**.
 
• It covers the President, Governors, Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts, Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and members of Parliament, among others.
 
• The schedule specifies the **salaries and allowances** for these officeholders to ensure transparency and uniformity.
 
• The provisions in this schedule are subject to amendments by Parliament as per constitutional needs.
 
• The Second Schedule is pivotal for maintaining the financial independence of constitutional authorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Schedules in Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution initially had **8 schedules**, which have now increased to 12.
 
• Schedules are used to provide detailed information on various provisions like administration, representation, and governance.
 
 
 
• **Second Schedule Details:**
 
 
• It ensures constitutional officeholders receive appropriate remuneration, promoting independence and impartiality.
 
• Officeholders like the President and Governors are barred from earning salaries from other sources during their tenure.
 
 
 
• **Related Articles:**
 
 
• Articles 59 and 158 restrict the President and Governors from holding any other profit-making positions.
 
• Articles 125 and 221 deal with the salaries of Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Amendments:**
 
 
• The Second Schedule can be amended by Parliament to adjust emoluments as per changing economic and administrative needs.
 
• Such amendments help maintain the financial viability of these provisions.
